overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a clear audience preference for extreme, high-stakes space phenomena and hypothetical 'What If' scenarios regarding alien worlds and extreme planetary conditions. Specifically, videos covering planetary anomalies (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets like TrES-2b, and extreme atmospheric phenomena) generate significantly higher velocity, views-per-day, and engagement (likes-per-view) compared to general psychological tricks or older standard space facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) lead in recent views (near or above 1,000) and maintain high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical scenarios involving extreme planetary environments using the 'What If You Fell Into...' hook framework.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring rare cosmic extremes such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) achieve top-tier view velocity and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Focus upcoming space content on bizarre, visually striking exoplanets and cosmic paradoxes that challenge common physical assumptions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal psychological phenomena, such as 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s), underperformed significantly with very low view counts and minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract internal psychological tricks unless tied to an extreme survival or high-concept sci-fi narrative.
